newsitem.title: ESTONIA: Estonian cen.bank denies will end currency board.
newsitem.headline: Estonian cen.bank denies will end currency board.

text.p: Estonia's central bank on Friday denied a report that the country would be forced to abandon its currency board system of pegging the kroon to the German mark when fellow Baltic state Lithuania ends its currency board.
The bank denied a report in the Financial Times, quoting Deutsche Bank, that Estonia would have to abandon the currency board when Lithuania starts a freer currency regime.
"The Bank of Estonia is confident that the currency board based monetary regime will not be changed within the next few years (far less within the next six months)," the bank said in a statement.
"The monetary systems, economic environment and institutional setup in the three Baltic states are far from identical," the bank added.
"There is no reason why any policy decision taken by one of the three would have to be copied by the other two," it said.
Under the currency board, the kroon is pegged at eight to one German mark.
Lithuania plans to end the currency board, whereby any rise in local in circulation has to be backed with a proportional rise in hard currency reserves.
The currency board provided confidence in both the Estonian kroon and the Lithuanian litas and helped dampen inflation.
But Lithuania says it has helped decrease the competitiveness of its exports by leading to a real appreciation of the currency.
It plans to end the board and let the central bank once more manage the fixed exchange rate of four litas to one dollar via open market operations and interest rate changes.
Estonia has often said it has no plans to change the currency board and its effectiveness and necessity is rarely if ever questioned by politicians or financiers.
